accepted.s: The under-construction Polavaram hydro project of APGENCO is associated with which of the following combinations?
o: Sileru River and 460 MW
Godavari River and 960 MW
Krishna River and 815.6 MW
Machkund River and 114.75 MW
accepted.x: The Polavaram hydro project is located on the Godavari and has an installed capacity of 12 × 80 MW, or 960 MW.
accepted.tq: Use the project–river–capacity combination to distinguish closely related hydro projects.
accepted.sec: AP hydro projects - river and installed capacity  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
With reference to hydroelectric projects in Andhra Pradesh, consider the following pairs:
1. Upper Sileru — 240 MW
2. Lower Sileru — 460 MW
3. Machkund — 114.75 MW
4. Polavaram — 815.6 MW
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
o: 1, 2 and 3 only
1 and 4 only
2 and 3 only
accepted.x: Upper Sileru has 240 MW, Lower Sileru 460 MW and Machkund 114.75 MW. Polavaram has 960 MW, not 815.6 MW.
accepted.tq: Check each numerical pairing against the project capacity before selecting the coded combination.
accepted.sec: AP hydro projects - river and installed capacity  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Upper Sileru hydroelectric project is located on which river, and its weir is at which place?
o: Godavari; Polavaram
Sileru; Guntawada
Machkund; Balimela
Krishna; Srisailam
accepted.x: The Upper Sileru project is on the Sileru River, with its weir at Guntawada.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the river name and the associated project location.
accepted.sec: AP hydro projects - river and installed capacity  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Srisailam hydroelectric project is correct?
o: Its Right Bank Power House has 770 MW in Andhra Pradesh and its Left Bank Power House has 900 MW in Telangana.
Its Right Bank Power House has 900 MW in Andhra Pradesh and its Left Bank Power House has 770 MW in Telangana.
It is situated on the Godavari River and has a total capacity of 960 MW.
Both its Right Bank and Left Bank Power Houses are located in Andhra Pradesh.
accepted.x: Srisailam is on the Krishna River. Its Right Bank Power House in Andhra Pradesh has 770 MW and its Left Bank Power House in Telangana has 900 MW.
accepted.tq: Use the bank-wise and State-wise capacity distinction to avoid reversing the two power houses.
accepted.sec: AP hydro projects - river and installed capacity  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Nagarjuna Sagar hydroelectric project:
1. It is situated on the Krishna River.
2. Its Main Power House has a capacity of 815.6 MW in Telangana.
3. Its Right Canal Power House has a capacity of 90 MW in Andhra Pradesh.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 only
1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Nagarjuna Sagar is on the Krishna, with a 815.6 MW Main Power House in Telangana and a 90 MW Right Canal Power House in Andhra Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Test a project through its river, location and component capacities together.
accepted.sec: AP hydro projects - river and installed capacity  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Machkund hydroelectric project is best described as which of the following?
o: A 960 MW project on the Godavari River
A 240 MW project wholly owned by Andhra Pradesh
A 460 MW project jointly operated by Andhra Pradesh and Telangana
A 114.75 MW joint project of Andhra Pradesh and Odisha
accepted.x: Machkund has an installed capacity of 114.75 MW and is a joint project of Andhra Pradesh and Odisha.
accepted.tq: Identify the exact capacity and inter-State partnership rather than the neighbouring Sileru capacities.
accepted.sec: AP hydro projects - river and installed capacity  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Chitrakonda (Balimela) Dam Toe Power House has which of the following characteristics?
o: 2 × 115 MW and an AP-Karnataka agreement for Lower Sileru
4 × 60 MW and an AP-Telangana agreement for Srisailam
12 × 80 MW and an AP-Odisha agreement for Polavaram
2 × 30 MW and an AP-Odisha agreement for renovation and modernisation of Machkund
accepted.x: The Chitrakonda (Balimela) Dam Toe Power House has 2 × 30 MW capacity. The October 2020 AP-Odisha agreement concerns R&M of Machkund, to be undertaken jointly by APGENCO and OHPC.
accepted.tq: Match the small power-house capacity with the specific inter-State agreement and agencies.
accepted.sec: AP hydro projects - river and installed capacity  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following statements about recent energy planning in Andhra Pradesh is NOT correct?
o: A 1,200 MW pumped-storage project has been approved in Kurnool in January 2026.
APGENCO plans two 3,200 MW ultra-mega supercritical plants at Srikakulam and Talcher.
The APERC-approved resource plan envisages 11,544 MW of additional capacity in five years.
The Talcher plant is proposed as a pithead plant, likely as a joint venture with Coal India.
accepted.x: A 1,200 MW pumped-storage project was approved in Kurnool in January 2026, but it is not described as an ultra-mega supercritical project. The other statements correctly describe the plans.
accepted.tq: Find the statement that wrongly transfers the technology description to a different project.
accepted.sec: AP hydro projects - river and installed capacity  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following is correctly matched?

Project — Capacity or feature
o: Simhadri — Thermal, Visakhapatnam, 2,000 MW
Rayalaseema TPP — Thermal, Muddanur, 2,560 MW
Dr NTTPS — Thermal, Vijayawada, 1,650 MW
Krishnapatnam Stage I — Hydro, Nellore, 1,600 MW

accepted.tq: Start with the sure plant–place pair and reject options that swap plant type or capacity.

accepted.s: The Stage V unit of Dr NTTPS mentioned in the power-sector data has which of the following specifications?
o: 2 × 115 MW, commissioned in April 2025
1 × 800 MW, commissioned in December 2023
1 × 650 MW, commissioned in December 2020
2 × 800 MW, commissioned in January 2026
accepted.x: Stage V of Dr NTTPS consists of one 800 MW unit commissioned in December 2023.
accepted.tq: Separate the stage-wise unit capacity and commissioning date from the plant’s total capacity.

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding small hydro in Andhra Pradesh is correct?
o: Small hydro includes all projects above 25 MW.
Small hydro capacity in Andhra Pradesh is 240 MW.
Only 10.5 MW has been installed under AP small hydro.
Small hydro capacity is identical to the State’s total pumped-storage capacity.
accepted.x: The installed capacity under small hydro in Andhra Pradesh is only 10.5 MW.
accepted.tq: Use the exact State-level figure and reject inflated capacities from larger projects.
accepted.sec: AP hydro projects - river and installed capacity  [APPSC]

accepted.s: In a hydroelectric power plant, which sequence correctly represents the conversion of energy?
o: Electrical energy → potential energy → kinetic energy → mechanical energy
Potential energy → kinetic energy → mechanical energy of turbine → electrical energy
Kinetic energy → chemical energy → mechanical energy → electrical energy
Mechanical energy → potential energy → thermal energy → electrical energy
accepted.x: Stored water has potential energy; falling water gains kinetic energy, turns the turbine through mechanical energy, and the generator produces electricity by electromagnetic induction.
accepted.tq: Follow the physical sequence from stored water to turbine motion and then generation.
accepted.sec: Energy conversion in a hydroelectric plant  [APPSC]

accepted.s: A hydroelectric plant uses stored water in a reservoir, whose release can be regulated to meet changing electricity demand. Such a plant is classified as a:
o: Storage or reservoir plant
Tidal plant
Run-of-the-river plant
Pumped-storage plant only
accepted.x: A storage or reservoir plant uses a dam to store water and regulate power output.
accepted.tq: Identify the plant type from its operational feature rather than from its energy source.
accepted.sec: Energy conversion in a hydroelectric plant  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes a run-of-the-river hydroelectric plant?
o: It requires a very large reservoir and completely changes the watercourse.
It operates only with nuclear-generated electricity.
It uses natural river flow with little or no storage and does not require a large dam or reservoir.
It stores surplus electricity by pumping water uphill.
accepted.x: Run-of-the-river plants use the natural flow of water with little or no storage and require no large dam or reservoir.
accepted.tq: Distinguish run-of-the-river generation from reservoir and pumped-storage systems.
accepted.sec: Energy conversion in a hydroelectric plant  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Pumped-storage hydropower functions most appropriately as which of the following?
o: A run-of-the-river system that avoids all storage
A thermal plant that converts coal directly into electricity
A grid battery that stores surplus power by pumping water uphill and releases it during peak demand
A dam designed only for flood control and not power generation
accepted.x: Pumped storage uses surplus electricity to pump water to an upper reservoir and releases it during peak demand; it is regarded as a grid battery and a fast large-scale storage option.
accepted.tq: Infer the technology from the charge–discharge cycle and its grid function.
accepted.sec: Energy conversion in a hydroelectric plant  [APPSC]

accepted.s: According to the classification specified for hydro projects, which statement is correct?
o: Small hydro means projects above 25 MW, while large hydro means projects up to 3 MW.
Small hydro means projects up to 25 MW, while large hydro means projects above 25 MW.
Large hydro is defined as projects between 3 MW and 25 MW only.
Both small and large hydro are limited to projects below 3 MW.
accepted.x: MNRE treats projects up to 25 MW as small hydro, while the Ministry of Power treats projects above 25 MW as large hydro.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between adjacent threshold categories using the exact numerical cutoff.
accepted.sec: Energy conversion in a hydroelectric plant  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which sequence correctly represents the change in the small-hydro threshold mentioned in the policy history?
o: Up to 25 MW in 1989 and up to 3 MW in November 1999
Up to 3 MW in 1989 and up to 25 MW in November 1999
Up to 3 MW in 1999 and up to 25 MW in 2005
Up to 25 MW in 1989 and above 25 MW in November 1999
accepted.x: The threshold was moved up to 3 MW in 1989 and subsequently to 25 MW in November 1999.
accepted.tq: Arrange policy changes by date and verify the associated numerical threshold.
accepted.sec: Energy conversion in a hydroelectric plant  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding India’s hydroelectric potential:
1. The estimated potential is more than 145 GW.
2. Approximately 36% of this potential has been developed.
3. Small-hydro potential is estimated at 21,133 MW at 7,133 sites.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: India’s hydro potential is estimated at more than 145 GW, about 36% is developed, and small-hydro potential is 21,133 MW across 7,133 sites.
accepted.tq: Retain all three scale indicators—total potential, developed share and small-hydro sites.
accepted.sec: Energy conversion in a hydroelectric plant  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under the Small Hydro Power Development Scheme for 2026–27 to 2030–31, the proposed financial outlay and additional capacity are respectively:
o: ₹1,500 crore and approximately 2,584.60 MW
₹2,400 crore and approximately 20,000 MW
₹3,600 crore and approximately 2,000 MW
₹2,584.60 crore and approximately 1,500 MW
accepted.x: The scheme proposes an outlay of ₹2,584.60 crore and approximately 1,500 MW of additional capacity.
accepted.tq: Pair the scheme period with its exact outlay and capacity target.
accepted.sec: Energy conversion in a hydroelectric plant  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly states the assistance pattern under the Small Hydro Power Development Scheme?
o: ₹3.6 crore/MW or 30% in the North-East and border areas, subject to a ₹30 crore cap; ₹2.4 crore/MW or 20% elsewhere, subject to a ₹20 crore cap
20% assistance only for projects in border areas
30% assistance without any monetary ceiling throughout India
₹2.4 crore/MW or 20% in the North-East and border areas, subject to a ₹20 crore cap; ₹3.6 crore/MW or 30% elsewhere, subject to a ₹30 crore cap
accepted.x: Higher assistance is available in the North-East and border areas—₹3.6 crore/MW or 30%, capped at ₹30 crore. Elsewhere it is ₹2.4 crore/MW or 20%, capped at ₹20 crore.
accepted.tq: Compare region, rate, alternative per-MW amount and ceiling without reversing the two slabs.
accepted.sec: Energy conversion in a hydroelectric plant  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT a major trade-off associated with large dams?
o: Displacement of project-affected communities
Sedimentation reducing reservoir capacity
Seismic risk in the Himalayan region
Improved migration routes for riverine fish without intervention
accepted.x: Large dams can block fish migration rather than improve it. Displacement, sedimentation and Himalayan seismic risk are recognised concerns.
accepted.tq: Identify the option that reverses an ecological impact of dams.
accepted.sec: Large dams - trade-offs, anti-dam movements, 'temples of modern India'  [other exams]

accepted.s: Between 1950 and 1990, approximately how many people were affected by projects associated with displacement, according to the cited assessment?
o: 1.85 million
3.3 million
18.5 million
185 million
accepted.x: The cited figure is 18.5 million people affected by projects during 1950–1990; more than 3,300 dams were built during the period considered.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the stated million-scale figure from nearby-looking alternatives.
accepted.sec: Large dams - trade-offs, anti-dam movements, 'temples of modern India'  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Which of the following is correctly matched?

Movement — Associated fact
o: Narmada Bachao Andolan — Opposition to the Sardar Sarovar project on the Narmada
Rally for the Valley — Anti-Tehri movement led by Sunderlal Bahuguna
Anti-Tehri dam movement — Campaign against the Sardar Sarovar project
Silent Valley Movement — Resettlement campaign for the Narmada displaced
accepted.x: Narmada Bachao Andolan opposed the Sardar Sarovar project on the Narmada. Rally for the Valley was an NBA campaign, while the anti-Tehri movement was associated with Sunderlal Bahuguna.
accepted.tq: Begin with the project–movement pair and reject swaps between Narmada, Tehri and Silent Valley.
accepted.sec: Large dams - trade-offs, anti-dam movements, 'temples of modern India'  [other exams]

accepted.s: Rally for the Valley, held in 1999, was associated with which issue?
o: Launching the Small Hydro Power Development Scheme
Opposing all wind-energy projects in India
Highlighting the resettlement of people displaced by the Narmada project
Promoting nuclear power in coastal Andhra Pradesh
accepted.x: Rally for the Valley was an NBA campaign that highlighted the resettlement concerns of people displaced by the Narmada project.
accepted.tq: Link the movement’s date and campaign objective rather than confusing it with another anti-dam movement.

accepted.s: Who described large dams such as Bhakra Nangal as the “temples of modern India”?
o: Mahatma Gandhi
Medha Patkar
Sunderlal Bahuguna
Jawaharlal Nehru
accepted.x: Jawaharlal Nehru used the expression “temples of modern India” for large dams such as Bhakra Nangal.
accepted.tq: Match the quotation with its speaker and the associated dam-development context.
accepted.sec: Large dams - trade-offs, anti-dam movements, 'temples of modern India'  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which of the following benefits of large dams most directly supports balancing fluctuations in electricity demand?
o: Prevention of all seismic activity
Permanent elimination of reservoir sedimentation
Flexible power generation for grid stability
Unrestricted fish migration
accepted.x: Large hydropower projects can provide flexible power generation, which helps maintain grid stability. They do not eliminate sedimentation, ecological disruption or seismic risk.
accepted.tq: Match the stated benefit to the specific operational requirement of the power grid.
accepted.sec: Large dams - trade-offs, anti-dam movements, 'temples of modern India'  [other exams]

accepted.s: Why is hydro-electricity identified as a source suitable for sustainable development in the cited comparison?
o: It has no land or ecological impacts during construction.
It requires no water storage or river flow.
It is cheap and clean once built.
It produces electricity only during floods.
accepted.x: Hydroelectricity is regarded as cheap and clean once the project has been built, although large projects can still involve displacement and ecological trade-offs.
accepted.tq: Select the precise benefit while rejecting absolute claims about environmental impacts.
accepted.sec: Large dams - trade-offs, anti-dam movements, 'temples of modern India'  [other exams]

o: November 1999
March 2019
December 2023
October 2020

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding hydropower potential in the North-Eastern region is correct?
o: Arunachal Pradesh has significant untapped hydropower potential, including the 2,000 MW Subansiri Lower project.
Arunachal Pradesh’s major potential is limited to pumped storage in Kurnool.
Subansiri Lower is a 25 MW small-hydro project in Kerala.
The North-Eastern region has no major untapped hydropower potential.
accepted.x: Arunachal Pradesh is identified as having large untapped hydropower potential, and Subansiri Lower is cited as a 2,000 MW project.
accepted.tq: Use the region–project–capacity combination to avoid mixing North-Eastern and Andhra Pradesh projects.
